about: Composition of the 0.2.0 release line: the core and the C/Python bindings of the working tree, pinned per file by git blob id in core.manifest and bindings.manifest, the packaging and acceptance tooling. 2026-10-10: squashed onto v0.1.0 for the public preview; the manifest replaced the base-revision comparison. 2026-10-11: repinned for the Zig 0.17.0 migration and the CPython 3.12-3.15 preparation (Py_LIMITED_API 0x030C0000, abi3 floor cp312); python/bolorgir/_core.c repinned for the explicit (PyObject *) casts of the limited-API build under GCC 14 (manylinux_2_28). Later on 2026-10-11: the line absorbs the session rollback and draft validation (ADR-0014: blg_session_create_ex, blg_session_rollback, blg_validate_tokens; the three symbols join the base ABI), the standalone regex constraint (ADR-0015, BLG_CONSTRAINT_REGEX, src/regex.zig) and the vLLM backend with its pinned patch and agent-evaluation material (ADR-0016, integrations/vllm, benchmarks/agent_eval); core and bindings manifests repinned accordingly and the implemented paths leave later_line_absent. Later on 2026-10-11 the review of 454c460 was closed: the adapter's draft validation follows the terminal-token set of the mask and acceptance path, a refused rollback leaves the session untouched, the structural-tag kernel (src/structtag.zig, BLG_CONSTRAINT_STRUCTURAL_TAG) implements the 9.2 subset, the backend writes blg-agent-trace/2 traces, and the checks are reproduced against one measured candidate; the core and bindings manifests were repinned again (candidate core 374738d4887746b3e4a09a34963ca252c67f59762b75b4bb834274ff118aef67, x86_64 baseline, the flags below). The R6 verdict of record for the earlier core (6e62e0d1) stays historical; the fresh R6 review of the then-current release-line core 9a5baf3e is admitted from the saved T3 data with the owner's D4 decisions of 2026-10-13 (t3-9a5baf3e/review-2). Per the owner's rules the final gate fields stay null until T8a is accepted and the owner sets them, and the preview block keeps its historical 6e62e0d1 binding. Remaining later-line items: ADR-0013 (interop numbers), ADR-0017 (bounded whitespace), the platform workflows and the tokenizer survey/metaspace work (T13/T14 queue). Later on 2026-10-11 the second review of f2dd6ad was closed: a partial begin of tags_with_separator (and of the first optional tag) no longer leaves the document endable, the nested parameters schema applies the same ADR-0005 completion filter as the standalone JSON constraint (dead-end prefixes like '-' under minimum 10 are withheld from the mask, cut drafts and refused by accept), the backend trace names the active structural-tag segment (the read-only blg_session_struct_segment joins the base ABI; Session.struct_segment in Python), a speculative terminal defers the trace finish and is recorded by a rollback event, and the request-id mapping is explicit: the patch carries external_req_id onto the engine Request and passes both ids to compile_grammar, the trace is keyed by the exposed id and records the internal one. Core and bindings manifests were repinned again (candidate core 0b05154b29a337a8c7c26fb25e9f84fdc8ad2cb60e7c92aab72835bb63957ce5, x86_64 baseline, the flags below); the collector (qualify_stack) looks the trace up by the response id and recomputes the free-text constraint's tool-name fingerprint. Later on 2026-10-11 the third review of 0b05154b was closed: the completion filter treats an end-literal prefix as alive regardless of the JSON continuation (the digit starting an end like 99 after <c>42 is offered by the mask, accepted, draft-valid, and the same bytes close the tag whichever token split is sampled), the collector replays the accept/rollback history (a rollback beyond the accepted tokens or a contradictory terminal_undone reads as unknown) and splits a request id into one stream per response variant (parallel-sampling children {index}_{internal} must cover the response's choices, and every variant is qualified separately); the tree is fmt-clean again (zig fmt --check build.zig src: the enum-to-integer calls and one test line the previous commit left non-conforming are upgraded); core and bindings manifests were repinned again (candidate core 374153b944b67802ef34a9bbfd4e02917c7087fc54abfa47d0e6ac9293aa927a, x86_64 baseline, the flags below). The GPU stage of the T10 checks (2026-10-12) closed a serialization gap found on the pinned vLLM 0.31.0 stack: the pinned xgrammar builder rides its serialization fields on the wire (content: style=json, any_order=false, max_whitespace_cnt=null; triggered_tags and any_text: an empty excludes list; any_text: null max_tokens/max_chars caps) and the kernel refused them, so the forced tool modes (required, named, strict-tool auto) failed with an internal error; the kernel now accepts exactly those defaults and refuses any other value with the field offset; the same stage exposed a mask-walk defect: the structural-tag free-text walk kept one DFS frame per trie byte, so on the real Qwen tokenizer (61-byte tokens against max_stack 59) the first fill overran the pool and aborted the engine core; single-child chains now descend in place like the standalone mask (src/mask.zig), with an ABI regression test. Core manifest repinned (candidate core 9a5baf3e373ac9a7a048b6a2b9bffda2c1e1e3d2f62b4cc62e70785cc3490c41, x86_64 baseline, the flags below). Later on 2026-10-12 the review of that evidence (round 7) closed its four findings on the same candidate: controlled resource-limit failures during the request (the per-call work budget dies inside the mask fill, the session budget at the structural-tag allocation) with a surviving neighbour and an engine-statistics release audit; the forbidden-candidate probe with a concrete token id, a measured pre-mask advantage and the masked exclusion in both configurations; the batch row reorder with the request-to-row mapping and a replay audit of every applied mask; and the evidence binding to 9a5baf3e (run5 manifests plus live EngineCore maps records); the adapter gains the diagnostics behind these checks (BLG_AGENT_STATS snapshots, the budget override variables, the row field of mask events; python/bolorgir/vllm.py sha256 7bbee811..., the kernel sources unchanged). Two follow-ups of the intermediate review were closed by the round-7b re-runs: the resource-limit checks now also cover a failure while a healthy neighbour request is generating in the same engine batch (the limits re-runs pass 10/10 per mode; the stream keeps producing tokens after the failure and both sessions release) and the batch-row-reorder verdict orders the events by their positions in the shared trace JSONL (per-request seq counters restart at zero) with a built-in negative control; the recomputed evidence (reorder-nospec-run5b.json, reorder-spec-run5b.json, mask audit 2/2 + 25/25) comes from the frozen traces without new traffic. Full pytest runs are regression checks and do not replace the admitted R6 acceptance of the current core; a stable release additionally requires an adopted T8a and the owner's gate decision. The XGrammar compact comparison is complete (A3/A4 series of 2026-10-13, benchmarks/reports/20261013_xgrammar-compare-a3/). 2026-10-26: the core and bindings manifests are repinned to the publication tree (the mask fast-path, state-copy and certificate-cache work; src/diag.zig joins the core manifest). The repin keeps the sources gate in step with the tree; it is not an acceptance, the R6 verdict and the T8a report for this core do not exist yet, and gate.* and preview.* stay unchanged.

core.patch: the release-line fix: the open-object certificates of src/complete.zig (pattern keys, dependency doom, the maxProperties count), the reachability flags of src/grammar.zig, the owed-name key completion of src/synth.zig, the -Dstrip option of build.zig; the mask-path counters of src/diag.zig (not part of the ABI) come with the 2026-10-24 diagnostics work; its tests tests/test_open_object_dead_ends.py and tests/completion_reference.py, the isolated acceptance runner (benchmarks/t3/run_t3_accept.sh, t3_identity.py, acceptance_pins.json, acceptance-requirements.txt, tests/test_t3_accept_runner.py) and its CHANGELOG entries come with it

gate.about: Evidence for the final tag (T7b), set by the owner after the gates close: the R6 review verdict and the T8a report, both committed. The release workflow refuses a final tag while either is null, not positive, or bound to another core than the one it builds.

preview.about: GitHub pre-release of an rc tag (owner decision 2026-10-10: public preview 0.2.0rc1 before the final gate). The release workflow builds the core, requires it to be the candidate of this committed, admitted R6 review verdict, and creates a draft pre-release with the wheel, the sdist and SHA256SUMS; nothing goes to PyPI or TestPyPI. The full T8a stays open and the final gate above stays in force for the stable release.
